t: Which body initiated the 1966 reinsurance pools in India?
e: The Indian Insurance Companies Association initiated the Fire and Hull reinsurance pools in 1966; GIC was formed only in 1972.

t: The long-term Issuer Credit Rating (ICR) assigned to GIC Re by A.M. Best is
e: A.M. Best assigns GIC Re a long-term ICR of A- (Excellent), the same grade as its FSR.

t: FNCRIP stands for
o: Fertilizer and Nuclear Combined Risk Insurance Pool
Federal Nuclear Catastrophe Reinsurance Insurance Pool
Fire and Natural Calamity Reinsurance Indian Pool
e: FNCRIP is the FAIR Natural Catastrophe Reinsurance Pool managed by GIC Re, along with IMTRIP.

t: An insurer with net worth ₹5,000 crore wants to set its retention on a liability (non-property) risk by the thumb rule. The indicative range is
e: Non-property retention is 1-2% of net worth: 1% of ₹5,000 crore = ₹50 crore and 2% = ₹100 crore.

t: A stated advantage of facultative reinsurance is that it
o: can protect the insurer even when treaty capacity is full
is the fastest form to arrange
e: Facultative offers flexibility, custom terms and support for exceptional exposures, including when treaty capacity is exhausted.

t: Facultative placement is unsuitable for
o: a portfolio with many small risks
e: Facultative is slow and costly to arrange, so it does not suit portfolios of many small risks.

t: A portfolio loss withdrawal debits outgoing reinsurers with their proportion of
e: Portfolio loss withdrawal takes 90% or 100% of estimated outstanding losses from outgoing reinsurers; the same amount is credited as portfolio loss entry to incoming reinsurers.

t: A fac-oblig treaty is NOT considered secure enough to be relied upon as
o: additional capacity after treaties are exhausted
e: Fac-oblig gives additional automatic capacity but should not be relied on as the primary reinsurance.

t: A disadvantage of a fac-oblig treaty from the reinsurer's viewpoint is that
o: it loses the right to inspect records
it cannot decline poor risks offered by the cedant
e: Under fac-oblig the reinsurer must accept everything the cedant chooses to cede, so strong trust between the parties is required.

t: Under a 40% quota share treaty a claim of ₹10 lakh is settled. The reinsurer's share is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Quota share applies the fixed percentage to sum insured, premium and claims alike: 40% of ₹10 lakh = ₹4 lakh.

t: The Board-approved final reinsurance programme (or CEO declaration of no change) must be filed with IRDAI within
o: 90 days of the financial year end
30 days of the commencement of the financial year
e: Final programme/CEO declaration: within 30 days of FY commencement; draft programme: 45 days before; new or revised arrangements: within 15 days of Board approval.

t: A surplus treaty with retention ₹2 crore and 10 lines is in place. For a risk of SI ₹30 crore, the amount to be placed facultatively is
e: Treaty capacity = 10 × ₹2 crore = ₹20 crore; retention ₹2 crore; 30 − 2 − 20 = ₹8 crore needs facultative placement.

t: Surplus limit under a treaty can be decided on the basis of
e: Surplus cessions are made on either sum insured or PML basis; on PML basis more premium is retained.

t: Under a 20% quota share treaty, a risk of ₹200 crore produces a quota share cession of
e: 20% of ₹200 crore = ₹40 crore, as shown in the programme table.

t: In the variable quota share example, retention on a sum insured of ₹1,50,00,000 is 5%. The ceding insurer's share is
e: 5% of ₹1.5 crore = ₹7,50,000; the reinsurer takes ₹1,42,50,000.

t: In the programme table, a ₹25 crore risk (4% statutory cession, ₹5 crore retention, 20% quota share) leaves how much for the 1st surplus?
e: 1 + 5 + 5 = ₹11 crore; 25 − 11 = ₹14 crore goes to the 1st surplus.

t: In the programme table the 2nd surplus treaty consists of
o: 8 lines subject to a maximum of ₹35 crore
10 lines subject to a maximum of ₹40 crore
5 lines subject to a maximum of ₹25 crore
e: The 1st surplus is 10 lines (max ₹40 crore) and the 2nd surplus 8 lines (max ₹35 crore) on a ₹5 crore retention.

t: The two underlying bases on which a treaty can be written are
e: A treaty is either on risk attaching basis (follows policies incepting in the period) or loss occurring basis (covers losses in the period).

t: Under a stop loss cover with retention 85% and limit up to 120%, the actual loss ratio is 110%. The reinsurer bears
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The reinsurer pays the loss ratio above 85% up to 120%: 110 − 85 = 25%.

t: The bordereau is prepared by
o: the reinsurer for the ceding insurer
the ceding insurer for the reinsurer
GIC Re for the pool members
e: The ceding insurer provides the reinsurer with a bordereau listing the risks ceded to the treaty.

t: Premium on a risk specifically excluded from a treaty is
o: not included in the reinsurance premium
paid to the reinsurer as deposit premium
e: Only premium on risks within the treaty scope is ceded; excluded risks and return premiums are left out.

t: The level of ceding commission is decided by
o: the ceding insurer and the reinsurer by agreement
e: Ceding commission is negotiated between cedant and reinsurer; only commission on obligatory cessions has regulatory minima.

t: Which of the following is deducted in arriving at treaty profit for profit commission?
e: Treaty profit = earned premium − incurred claims − ceding commission.

t: Where a treaty is terminated for a cause other than the 90 days' notice, the insurer may make termination effective retroactively from
o: the first day of the next financial year
the date of the last bordereau
the inception date of the treaty
the last day of the previous quarter or 31st December of the current or previous year
e: The clause gives the insurer the option of a retroactive termination date as the circumstances warrant.

t: A reinsurer wishes to cut off its liability completely on the termination date of a proportional treaty. It does so by
o: paying the ceding insurer a portfolio withdrawal premium
e: A portfolio withdrawal premium paid by the reinsurer ends its liability for unexpired policies on termination.

t: A risk of sum insured ₹2 crore has a PML of 40%. With a retention of ₹20 lakh and cession on PML basis, the amount reinsured is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). PML = 40% of ₹2 crore = ₹80 lakh; reinsured = 80 − 20 = ₹60 lakh (3 lines).

t: Marine and aviation treaties account premium and losses
o: on a loss occurring basis only
to the calendar year of payment
e: Marine and aviation are written on underwriting year basis, so portfolio entry and withdrawal do not apply.

t: In non-proportional reinsurance the ceding insurer's retention is
o: a percentage of each sum insured
e: XL retention is a monetary amount called deductible, excess, priority or underlying.

t: Working XL is particularly effective for
o: aggregate loss ratio of crop insurance
e: Working XL covers day-to-day losses including single-event accidents and is effective for third-party liability.

t: A per-risk XL has a priority of ₹1 crore and limit of ₹5 crore. A loss of ₹7 crore occurs. The reinsurer pays and the cedant bears respectively
e: Reinsurer pays up to the limit above priority = ₹5 crore; the cedant bears the ₹1 crore priority plus the ₹1 crore above the layer = ₹2 crore.

t: OICL's catastrophe XL for all perils (non-marine) is
e: Cat XL all perils is ₹1,200 crore excess of ₹50 crore; the EQ-specific Cat XL is ₹2,900 crore xs ₹50 crore.

t: A stop loss treaty pays 90% of the loss ratio above 80% up to a maximum loss ratio of 130%. In a year with loss ratio 120%, the reinsurer pays
e: Excess over 80% is 40%; 90% of 40% = 36%.

t: Stop loss cover is usually expressed in
o: percentage terms of the loss ratio
e: Stop loss (excess of loss ratio) is expressed in percentages; aggregate XL expresses the same cover in amounts.

t: An insurer's retention per risk is ₹25 lakh and the PMN for one event is 8. Its retention per event is
e: Retention per risk = retention per event ÷ PMN, so retention per event = 25 lakh × 8 = ₹2 crore.

t: In relation to XL premium, a larger deductible (priority) results in
e: The higher the underlying retention, the lower the exposure to the reinsurer and hence the smaller the premium.

t: The rate on line for successive higher layers of an XL programme is
e: Rate on line (premium ÷ limit) declines for each successive higher layer as the probability of loss reduces.

t: A corporate agent may tie up with a maximum of how many insurers in each line of business?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Raised from 3 to 9 insurers per category (life, general, health) by the 2022 amendment to the Corporate Agents Regulations.

t: Under a burning cost rated XL cover, when the actual loss experience exceeds the maximum rate, the reinsurer
e: The agreed range caps the reinsured's cost at the maximum rate and floors it at the minimum rate.

t: Additional reinstatement premium may be charged on which bases?
o: Pro rata for the amount reinstated, pro rata for the remaining period, or a combination
On the basis of the rate on line only
e: Reinstatement premium can be pro rata to amount, pro rata to time, or both; risk XL gives the first two reinstatements free.

t: On a loss occurring basis XL contract, at termination the reinsurer
o: is not liable for losses occurring after termination, with no portfolio taken or withdrawn
is relieved of losses occurred but unsettled
remains liable until all policies expire
must pay a portfolio withdrawal premium
e: Loss occurring XL covers losses in the contract period only; it remains liable for losses occurred but not settled, and there is no portfolio transfer.

t: For marine business with wide variation in values per vessel, the preferred arrangement is
o: surplus, to secure automatic facility per bottom up to the maximum foreseeable extent
e: Surplus suits marine when values per vessel vary widely; quota share is used when exposures cluster around one level.

t: Engineering business is typically reinsured through
o: a combined quota share and surplus arrangement
e: The material lists engineering as combined quota share and surplus, aviation as facultative and miscellaneous as surplus.

t: The obligatory cession that Indian general insurers must make to GIC Re is currently:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The obligatory cession was reduced to 4% from 1 April 2022.

t: The original insured has no rights under the reinsurance contract because
o: the policy is stamped in India
there is no privity of contract between the insured and the reinsurer
the reinsurance is signed only by the reinsurer
e: The insured is not a party to the reinsurance contract; the subject matter of reinsurance is the reinsured's liability under the original contract.

t: A material change in the ownership or control of the other party gives a treaty party the right to
o: terminate the agreement immediately by notice
e: Immediate termination grounds include impossibility of performance, insolvency or loss of capital/authority, material change in ownership or control, and breach of terms.

t: Under the access to records clause, the reinsurer's inspection of the cedant's books is
o: permitted only after a claim dispute
at the reinsurer's own expense during office hours, and may be restricted to an appointed representative
at the cedant's expense at any time
e: The reinsurer may inspect any records of the ceding insurer at its own cost during office hours, possibly through an appointed representative.

t: A downgrade clause allows the reinsured to
o: cancel the reinsurance and seek a new reinsurer if the reinsurer is downgraded by rating agencies
e: The downgrade clause protects reinsurance security when the reinsurer's rating falls.

t: Fire and accident proportional reinsurance accounts are rendered on
o: an accounts year basis with premiums at original gross rates
an underwriting year basis net of acquisition cost
e: Fire and accident proportional treaties use the accounts year basis; marine proportional uses underwriting year with premiums net of acquisition costs.

t: Under a sliding scale commission, the rate of commission depends on
o: the loss ratio of the treaty during the treaty year
e: Sliding scale commission varies with the treaty's loss ratio = incurred losses × 100 ÷ earned premium.

t: An insurer cedes ₹800 crore of reinsurance premium outside India. Its maximum placement with a CBR rated AA is
e: AA is greater than A+, so the limit is 20% of ₹800 crore = ₹160 crore.
